result_text:
Per-extension entries are now named with the plain lower-cased extension (`java`, `js`, `xml`), and the codeanalyzer module's tests pass. I didn't run the other modules' tests or add a test for the landscape merge of old and new spellings.

- **`SourceCodeAspectUtils.getAspectsPerExtensions`** now names each aspect with the bare extension instead of `"  *.ext"`. This is what ends up in `linesOfCodePerExtension` and `fileCountPerExtension` in `analysisResults.json`.
- **`AnalysisUtils.analyze`** no longer strips the decoration when it builds the per-extension metric names, so the metric ids stay the same (`..._EXT_java` and so on). The indented `  *.ext: N files, …` lines of the textual summary keep their look because the prefix is added only there.
- **`LandscapeAnalysisResults`** has a new `getBareExtension` helper that trims a name, drops a leading `*.` and lower-cases it. `getLinesOfCodePerExtension` and `merge` both use it. Old `"  *.java"` data and new `"java"` data therefore land under one `java` entry, in the main scope and in the merged "other" category. Each repository appears once in a merged entry's breakdown.
- **Tests:** I updated `CodeConfigurationTest.getScopesWithExtensions` and the two `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` methods (`getAspectsPerExtensions`, `getAspectsPerExtensionsSorted`) to expect the bare names.

I left the `.replace("*.", "")` in `ReportFileExporter` (the `reports` module) alone. It still works on bare names, since there is nothing left to strip.
